business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Operations in Customs Free Trade Zones

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (Free Trade Zone Customs Bonded Depot Regime)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified commercial, customs and tax statutes; no binding stare decisis)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA), effective 15 May 2012
Colombia–European Union Multi-Party Trade Agreement, provisionally applied since August 2013
Colombia–Canada Free Trade Agreement, effective 15 August 2011
Double Taxation Agreement between Colombia and the Kingdom of Spain, in force
Double Taxation Agreement between Colombia and the Swiss Confederation, in force
Double Taxation Agreement between Colombia and the Republic of France, in force

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF creation); Ley 1121 de 2006 (AML/CFT); Ley 1258 de 2008 (S.A.S.); Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971); Ley 1004 de 2005; Decreto 2147 de 2016 (Free Trade Zones); Decreto 390 de 2016 (Customs Statute, bonded depots); Resolución DIAN 083 de 2023 (RUB – UBO registry); Decreto 1068 de 2015 (Unified Hacienda Regulation, AML/CFT implementing provisions).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granted by each non-resident shareholder or UBO for execution of the S.A.S. incorporation and free zone authorization filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin (or Colombian notary where executed locally)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the country of origin; if non-Hague Party, consular legalization at the Colombian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation of the parent company or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official Companies Registry or Chamber of Commerce in the parent's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the valid passport or national identity card of each UBO, legal representative and subscriber
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or notary public of the issuing State
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Hague Apostille or consular legalization; for Colombian nationals, notarization before a Colombian notary is sufficient

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate (antecedentes judiciales) of each legal representative, manager and each UBO over 5%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal records authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn translation into Spanish

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, officers, and shareholders before notarization and registry filing against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU restrictive measures, the Colombian consolidated LA/FT lists published by UIAF, and national/foreign PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs and persons connected with OFAC/UN/EU-sanctioned jurisdictions. Negative screening evidence must be kept in the corporate compliance file; any positive hit triggers a Suspicious Transaction Report (ROS) to UIAF under Ley 1121 de 2006 and UIAF reporting instructions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) – https://www.rue.com.co and the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) platform of the competent Cámara de Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be in Latin script; Spanish is the general statutory language, but foreign-language names are accepted if they are not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, do not use symbols or characters foreign to the Latin alphabet, and are complemented by the compulsory legal form suffix 'S.A.S.'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Cámara de Comercio refuses the name clearance, the applicant may file, within ten (10) business days after the decision is notified, a 'recurso de reposición' before the same Registrar and a 'recurso de apelación' before the Superintendencia de Sociedades, under Ley 1437 de 2011 and the registry rules. Where the rejection arises from a prohibited token, the applicant must obtain the relevant prior authorization from the competent ministry or DIAN (e.g., 'Zona Franca') and resubmit. Where the rejection is due to identical or similar name conflict, the applicant should propose a new distinctive name via a fresh homonimia application before the reservation expires or within the 30-day renewal if permitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted. The bonded warehouse/deposit business requires actual, physically secured, customs-controlled premises located inside an authorized Free Trade Zone (Zona Franca). Virtual office arrangements cannot support the mandatory DIAN inspection, goods custody, merchandise count, or customs document requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Quantified likelihood of at least one unannounced DIAN customs or police inspection in the first 12 months of operation is estimated at 70–75%, with additional mandatory periodic inspections by the Free Trade Zone operator under the authorization contract.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance certificate (Certificado de Homonimia) for the proposed S.A.S. name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the chosen domicile (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff published by the Cámara de Comercio / Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the incorporation instrument and shareholder powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff schedule regulated by the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration fees (Derechos de Inscripción) with the Cámara de Comercio based on initial subscribed capital of USD 50,000, including RUES issuance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Percentage scale applied by the Cámara de Comercio based on the subscribed/paid capital (Colombian statutory tariff)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration preparation and filing under Resolución DIAN 083 de 2023 (RUB) by local counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Engaged law firm (DIAN does not charge for the electronic RUB filing itself)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee for pre-incorporation AML/UBO advisory

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization of foreign corporate documents, powers of attorney, IDs and police certificates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the country of origin and Colombian Consulate (where applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Governmental apostille tariff in the source jurisdiction plus professional handling fee (market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Free Trade Zone operator qualification/admission fee and DIAN bonded depot authorization filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Free Trade Zone operator and DIAN (División de Régimen de Aduanas)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Operator's contractual tariff and DIAN administrative fees for customs bonded warehouse authorization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation of S.A.S. bylaws, corporate records, and initial AML/CFT compliance manual applicable to the bonded warehouse
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for pre-incorporation corporate and compliance drafting

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Colombian Political Constitution Art. 333 (free enterprise); Código de Comercio, Arts. 110, 353-356 and 373 (commercial companies and corporate purpose); Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada regime), Arts. 5, 12 and 29; Decree 1074 of 2015 (single regulatory decree on trade and company registration); Decree 2147 of 2016 and Decree 278 of 2018 (free trade zone users); Decree 390 of 2016 (customs statute) and applicable DIAN Resolutions on bonded depots.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered domicile, operating through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES); integrated NIT enrollment with Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); external supervision by Superintendencia de Sociedades when asset thresholds are exceeded.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) recorded in the Registro Mercantil and certified by the issuance of the Certificado de Cámara de Comercio, leading to the activation of the NIT (tax ID).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum subscribed or paid-up capital for S.A.S. formation under Law 1258 of 2008; capital may be payable in 2 years, with payment terms stated in the bylaws. For the user of a permanent free trade zone operating a bonded depot, the qualifying net equity must evidence total assets minus liabilities of at least approximate USD 125,000 (equity requirement of Decree 2147/2016) and customs guarantee coverage is assessed by DIAN, not by the Chamber of Commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION No. 1 OF THE FOUNDING BOARD OF [CORPORATE NAME] S.A.S. — WHEREAS the incorporation document was approved and the authorized capital fully subscribed; the board convened with full quorum. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED: 1. Ratify the subscription and two-year payment schedule of all issued shares. 2. Adopt as the registered corporate seat the premises at [address] within the Free Trade Zone, Department of [department]. 3. Appoint [Full Name] as sole legal representative and [Full Name] as principal accountant. 4. Instruct the legal representative to file the Chamber of Commerce registration, DIAN tax enrollment, free trade zone user application and customs bonded-depot authorization, and to open the corporate bank account. Certified as adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs Bonded Depot Authorization (Habilitación como Depósito Aduanero en Zona Franca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN, Directorate of Customs Management (Dirección de Gestión de Aduanas)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply under Decree 390 of 2016 for the authorization of the depot as an authorized bonded warehouse inside the free trade zone. Submit the facility technical sheet, inventory management system, handling control procedures, insurance and customs guarantee bond (póliza de garantía), and signal the customs insertion points for electronic filings. DIAN inspects the facility if necessary and issues the habilitación resolution.
required_dossiers: Copy of the MinCIT user qualification resolution
Technical facility layout of the bonded warehouse
Customs guarantee bond and insurance certificates
Inventory management and traceability system SOPs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the application, file corrective evidence within the 1-month reopening term; use the consulta aduanera instrument to resolve legal uncertainties, and exhaust recursos administrativos before seeking judicial protection before the Contencioso Administrativo tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio, Industria y Turismo (MinCIT), Comité de Zonas Francas; customs operation and deposit authorization jointly under DIAN, Dirección de Gestión de Aduanas
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Habilitación como Depósito Aduanero Permanente en Zona Franca (Bonded Depot Authorization) and Calificación como Usuario de Zona Franca para Depósito de Almacenamiento

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) or the Regional Autonomous Corporation (CAR) with jurisdiction over the free trade zone locality
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Environmental Registration (Registro Ambiental) and spatial compatibility certificate; a full EIA is not mandatory for non-extractive bonded storage/logistics activities, but the facility must obtain the environmental compatibility approval from the zone operator's global environmental license or a standalone environmental declaration under Decree 1076 of 2015.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Resolution 0631 of 2015: pH 6.0-9.0, total suspended solids below 50 mg/L, BOD5 below 20 mg/L. Air emissions for VOCs and particulate matter are controlled per Resolution 909 of 2008 and Title V of Decree 1076 of 2015. Hazardous waste management requires waste manifests and storage control under Decree 4741 of 2005, Law 1259 of 2008 for solid waste segregation, and regulator-verified disposal contracts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety requires a technical fire-safety certificate (Certificado de Cumplimiento de Normas de Seguridad Humana) issued by the municipal fire department, including fire-suppression systems, hydrant network, and evacuation signage. Structural load clearance is obtained through the Reglamento Colombiano de Construcción Sismo Resistente (NSR-10) structural inspection and report signed by a licensed structural engineer. Occupational workplace clearance requires registration of the SG-SST (Safety and Health at Work) program with the Ministry of Labor under Law 1562 of 2012 and Decree 1072 of 2015, including emergency drills, medical surveillance, and risk assessments for logistics-storage workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), attached to the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit. Primary portal: www.dian.gov.co; transactional and registration portal: MUISCA (muisca.dian.gov.co); electronic invoicing services: 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica' via DIAN authorized web services and software providers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step-by-step for a foreign-owned S.A.S. operating a bonded depot in a Colombian free trade zone: (1) Incorporate the S.A.S. through the Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) and obtain the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal; (2) obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) — assigned automatically by DIAN at incorporation, or filed through MUISCA/DIAN by a duly appointed local legal representative (apoderado) for foreign non-resident entities; (3) complete and keep current the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) identifying income tax liability, VAT (IVA) liability as 'Régimen Común', customs status, and free-trade-zone user status; (4) obtain the bonded warehouse authorization as 'depósito aduanero permanente' or free-trade-zone user certification through DIAN's customs authority and the Comité de Zonas Francas; (5) activate the electronic invoicing system ('habilitación de facturación electrónica') with DIAN before commencing taxable operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no US-style check-the-box regime; the S.A.S. is per se a resident corporation under Estatuto Tributario Article 12. Available statutory elections: (a) Free Trade Zone industrial-user certification under Law 1004/2005 and Decrees 2147/2016 and 659/2018, enabling the preferential 20% corporate income tax rate under ET Article 240-1 instead of the general 35% rate; (b) election to apply the unified 'Régimen SIMPLE' under ET Articles 905 ff., though unavailable to free-trade-zone users and therefore inapplicable to this entity; (c) election to file consolidated income tax returns with a Colombian corporate group under ET Article 23-1; (d) election of IFRS-based tax recognition criteria for the opening and subsequent tax periods; (e) mandatory, non-elective hybrid mismatch, CFC, and dual-resident tie-breaker rules under Law 2010/2019 and ET Articles 884-891.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no monetary turnover threshold for habitual business sellers: VAT responsibility arises from the first transaction once activity is habitual. The de minimis exclusion under ET Article 437 applies only to isolated/occasional sales or sellers of exclusively exempt goods where total proceeds in the prior or current calendar year do not exceed 3,500 UVT (approximately COP 174.3 million for 2025, with UVT set at COP 49,799). A bonded warehouse operator in a free trade zone engages in habitual commercial operations and must register as a full 'Régimen Común' VAT responsible entity through the RUT from inception.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory. The 'Factura Electrónica de Venta' (FEV) must be transmitted in real time to DIAN through certified software via REST/SOAP APIs and prior validation ('validación previa') before the invoice is made available to the buyer, in accordance with Resolution 000165/2023, Resolution 000042/2020, and Decree 2242/2015. Each invoice must carry the Código Único de Facturación Electrónica (CUFE) or Código Único de Documento Soporte (CUDS), a QR code, and the DIAN electronic validation response. Export invoices must include the applicable exchange/export codes and reference the customs export declaration. Invoices transmitted without authorization, or not transmitted, deprive the buyer of input VAT credit and expense deduction rights and expose the seller to administrative fines under ET Articles 652 and 652-10.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods admitted into, stored within, and removed from the Colombian free trade zone to a third-country destination are treated as exports for VAT purposes; the introduction of goods from the national customs territory into the free trade zone is itself characterized as an export. Bonded warehouse, storage, handling, and ancillary services physically performed inside the free trade zone exclusively for registered free-trade-zone users and used exclusively within the zone perimeter are deemed 'exportación de servicios' under ET Article 481 and are subject to VAT at 0%. The supplier must prove the recipient's valid FTZ user status, the physical location of the service within the FTZ, and the direct relationship between the service and the FTZ user's authorized or industrial purpose. Input VAT attributable to such zero-rated export services is creditable and refundable through DIAN's periodic VAT returns, including where export transactions exceed taxable domestic transactions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DEX) validated in the DIAN SIGLO XXI / VUCE customs platform authorizing physical exit from the free trade zone
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or road transport document evidencing physical departure to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas) showing settlement through an authorized Colombian financial intermediary
Electronic export invoice (FEV) bearing the CUFE code, export tariff classification, and reference to the DEX number
Free trade zone entry/exit inventory register and authorized bonded warehouse operator records (kárdex de inventarios and warehouse authorization)
Free trade zone user certificate, commercial invoice, packing list, and, where applicable, certificate of origin
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN conducts cross-system audits matching the customs DEX, FTZ inventory records, electronic invoices, and foreign exchange repatriation filings. If export proceeds are not repatriated within the mandatory 180-day term, or if physical export is not substantiated, DIAN retroactively disallows the 0% VAT treatment, assesses 19% VAT on the transaction value plus daily moratory interest under ET Articles 634 and 635, applies the inexactness penalty of up to 100%–200% of the omitted tax under ET Article 648 as reformed by Law 2277/2022, and may impose fines of 5,000–10,000 UVT for false export documentation. Where zero-rating is obtained fraudulently or the goods never leave the FTZ, criminal liability for contraband under Law 1762/2015 may attach. In addition, loss of the FTZ user certificate allows DIAN to claw back the preferential 20% corporate income tax rate and all VAT benefits for the entire noncompliant period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Banco de la República), acting jointly with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) and the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN), administers the Colombian foreign-exchange regime (Régimen de Cambios Internacionales) under Decree 1068 of 2015 and Circular Reglamentaria Externa DCIN-83 of Banco de la República. All cross-border currency transactions must be channelled through an authorised foreign-exchange intermediary (Intermediario del Mercado Cambiario, IMC), namely a commercial bank supervised by the SFC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is freely convertible for both current-account and capital-account operations; Colombia imposes no exchange controls, currency auctions, or differential exchange-rate bands. Current-account items are fully convertible and require only channelling through an IMC, including dividend remittances, interest, royalties, software and BPO service export proceeds, and trade settlements. Capital-account foreign direct investment (FDI) is likewise unrestricted in amount, but the equity contribution must be channelled through an IMC using the Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional (Formulario No. 4) and registered with Banco de la República's Registro de Inversiones Internacionales; such registration is the legal precondition for future dividend remittance and capital repatriation. Profit remittance hurdles are documentary rather than quantitative: the company must evidence paid and settled corporate income tax, submit audited financial statements, produce the shareholders' meeting minutes approving the dividend, and present the FDI registration certificate, all channelled under the applicable current-account exchange declaration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombia does not impose any mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds, meaning there is no statutory percentage surrender of export receipts into COP. However, all proceeds from exports of goods and services must be repatriated and channelled through an authorised IMC within 12 months from the date of the export customs declaration (Declaración de Exportación, DEX) for goods, or within the agreed commercial payment term, capped at 12 months, for services; extensions are possible only upon justified application to Banco de la República. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency in a local foreign-currency account (cuenta en moneda extranjera), but every collection must be reported through the applicable Declaración de Cambio (Formulario No. 1 for goods exports, Formulario No. 3 for services exports). Non-compliance triggers administrative fines and legal sanctions under the Régimen Cambiario, and may additionally impair DIAN customs privilege for FTZ warehouse operators.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW. Cross-border fintech EMIs (e.g., Wise, Revolut, Airwallex) do not hold a Colombian banking licence nor an SFC foreign-exchange intermediary authorisation; they cannot lawfully open a Colombian current account, cannot file Declaraciones de Cambio, and cannot be used to channel export proceeds without breaching the FX regime. EMIs may be used only as a secondary auxiliary channel for minor cross-border vendor payments where no COP conversion occurs, provided the local tier-1 IMC bank remains the primary treasury and clearing rail with a segregated foreign-currency account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required for the account-opening KYC process: the legal representative (representante legal) or a duly appointed attorney-in-fact (apoderado) must attend an in-person verification interview at the bank in Colombia. Under SFC Circular Básica Jurídica Part 1 Title IV, enhanced due diligence is mandated for FTZ and bonded-depot entities, and remote video-identification may supplement but not replace the face-to-face meeting. For non-resident directors, the appointing corporate resolutions must be notarised and apostilled under the Hague Convention; certain banks additionally require a notarised power of attorney granted before a Colombian notary or at a Colombian consulate. In practice, at least one authorised signatory must travel to Bogotá or Medellín for the final account activation and biometric verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Free trade zone and bonded-depot status flagged as elevated money-laundering risk due to customs opacity and third-party goods storage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) DIAN resolution recognising the entity as a free-zone user and authorising the bonded warehouse; (2) current bonded-depot operating licence; (3) inventory ledgers by client and by customs declaration; (4) sample export declarations (DEX) and import declarations; (5) warehouse lease, storage and custody agreements; (6) customs brokerage and logistics contracts; (7) SAGRILAFT AML/CFT manual and transactional profile matrix; (8) audited financial statements with Colombian revisor fiscal opinion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholders create heightened beneficial-ownership (UBO) and PEP screening exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate chain-of-title documentation to ultimate natural persons; certificates of existence of foreign shareholders; apostilled board/shareholder resolutions appointing the local legal representative; updated shareholder register; sworn UBO declarations; tax-residency certificates; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for the initial capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border wire transfers exceeding the commercial profile of a domestic bonded warehouse.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed storage contracts and client invoices evidencing fee income; inventory procurement orders; three-year treasury projection matching FX inflows to warehouse revenue; monthly FX channelling report reconciled to Declaraciones de Cambio; bank-completed AML sectoral questionnaire; documented trade cycle for bonded imports and reexports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingling of software-outsourcing and digital-service revenue with bonded-inventory flows in a single treasury account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ERP cost-centre segregation; valid service-level agreements with offshore clients; export-of-services declarations and VAT-exemption certificates; treasury policy note explaining the multi-purpose use of the account; quarterly reconciliation of SWIFT purpose codes to the respective FX declarations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: foreign shareholders remit USD/EUR by SWIFT MT103 to the entity's foreign-currency account at a local IMC bank, specifying in SWIFT field 70 the Banco de la República concept code 4012 (Inversión Directa en Sociedades). The IMC converts at the Tasa Representativa del Mercado (TRM) or retains the foreign currency, and simultaneously files the Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional (Formulario No. 4). The investment is registered with Banco de la República's Registro de Inversiones Internacionales before any dividend remittance or capital repatriation. Evidentiary bundle: notarised shareholders' capitalisation minutes, amended bylaws registered with the Cámara de Comercio, updated certificate of existence and legal representation, and the DIAN FTZ-user resolution confirming the entity's bonded-depot authorisation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (a) cross-border supplier payments for bonded inventory are executed by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers or MT202 bank-to-bank transfers out of the bank's USD account, linked to the import invoice and reported on Formulario No. 2 (Importaciones de Bienes); (b) documentary trade settlements use commercial letters of credit (UCP600, sight or usance) issued by the IMC's trade desk against transport documents, invoices and customs declarations; (c) local COP disbursements for logistics, DIAN duties and customs brokers are cleared through ACH Colombia for low-value items and Banco de la República's high-value RTGS (Sistema de Pagos de Alto Valor, SPAV) for same-day settlements; (d) cross-border service payments (insurance, royalties, IT support) use Formulario No. 3 supported by contracts. All outbound payments preserve an audit trail from SWIFT purpose codes through the IMC's exchange declaration to the enterprise resource planning payment block.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/COP forward contracts (forwards on TRM) executed with a local IMC against a documented underlying commercial exposure such as bonded-inventory imports or dividend accruals.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/COP) for structural hedging of long-term USD procurement or refinancing obligations.
FX swaps combining a spot transaction with a forward reversal for short-term liquidity management in the bonded inventory cycle.
USD/COP over-the-counter options (calls and puts) purchased through an IMC for strict currency-risk cover with no speculative short positions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only when settled in COP cash through a local IMC and treated as hedges under IFRS; offshore non-IMC NDFs are not recognisable under the Régimen Cambiario and create un-enforceable FX audit exposure for the Colombian treasury.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registry renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil), including renewal of the bonded warehouse establishment registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) of the S.A.S.'s registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March each calendar year; covers commercial registration status as of 1 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a surcharge of up to 1.5% of the applicable annual tariff per month or fraction, capped at 100% of the tariff; non-renewal for two consecutive years permits cancellation of the commercial registry and referral to the Superintendencia de Sociedades

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, management report, and shareholders' approval minutes (Estados Financieros de fin de ejercicio y acta de asamblea de accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce; Superintendencia de Sociedades if the entity is subject to its surveillance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must approve the calendar-year financial statements by 31 March; the approved documents must be deposited with the Chamber of Commerce within one month thereafter (by 30 April)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit exposes the S.A.S. to registry fines, loss of good standing, and limitations on executing notarial and registry procedures; surveillance authorities may impose additional corrective measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and complementary return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios), including the computation of the preferential free-trade-zone income tax rate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales – DIAN
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual calendar published by DIAN; for legal entities the filing window is generally between September and October, allocated by the last two digits of the NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers penalty under Article 641 of the Tax Code at 5% of the tax due per month or fraction, up to 100%; if no tax is due, the penalty is calculated on gross assets or gross income, with interest and default surcharges accruing until filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Exogenous information annual return (Información Exógena / Medios Magnéticos)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales – DIAN
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual deadline set by DIAN resolution, generally falling between May and August of the following tax year according to NIT digits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate filing is penalized under Articles 651 and 651-1 of the Tax Code, up to 15,000 UVT (approximately USD 181,000 for 2024); extended non-compliance can result in additional monthly sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation (Registro de Beneficiario Final) submitted with the commercial registry renewal and DIAN beneficiary-owner database
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce; DIAN beneficial-owner registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the 31 March annual registry renewal; any change in beneficial ownership must be updated within one month after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or late beneficial-owner registration may result in monetary fines by the Chamber or DIAN, blockage of registry transactions, and adverse treatment in tax information-exchange cooperation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Free-trade-zone user's annual operating and inventory report (Informe Anual de Operaciones en Zona Franca) for the bonded warehouse depot
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Comité de Zonas Francas / Ministerio de Comercio, Industria y Turismo; operative copy to DIAN
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first quarter of each calendar year, generally by 31 March, for the preceding year; the exact date is fixed in the FTZ approval instrument and Comité instructions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing may lead to customs fines, suspension of the FTZ user's operating authorization, and an administrative procedure that could result in loss of free-trade-zone status

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is mandatory when total gross assets at the prior 31 December exceed 5,000 current legal monthly minimum wages (SMLMV), or gross income exceeds 3,000 SMLMV; it is also required if the S.A.S. is subject to surveillance by the Superintendencia de Sociedades, publicly offers securities, or is made subject to audit by the FTZ approval instrument. Below these thresholds, the S.A.S. may operate without a Revisor Fiscal unless the shareholders' agreement or financing covenants require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Colombia (NIIF), governed by Decreto 2420 of 2015 and subsequent amendments: Grupo 1 applies full NIIF/IFRS for large and publicly accountable entities; Grupo 2 applies NIIF para PYMES (IFRS for SMEs) for other S.A.S. entities; Grupo 3 applies simplified standards for micro-entities where eligible.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must keep a current register of ultimate beneficial owners, identifying every natural person that directly or indirectly owns at least 5% of the capital, votes, or exercises control through other means. The annual commercial registry renewal filed by 31 March includes confirmation that beneficial-owner data remains accurate; any transfer of shares, change in control, pledge, or death causing a change in the beneficial-owner chain must be reported to the registry within one month.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified Free Trade Zone users benefit from a reduced corporate income tax rate of 20% under Article 240-1 of the Colombian Tax Statute, instead of the standard 35%. Preferential treatment requires an FTZ operating license, DIAN certification, and compliance with export/warehousing activity tests.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) filed through DIAN electronic portal (Muisca - DIAN electronic filing system).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year follows the calendar year. The annual Form 110 must be filed according to the DIAN Resolution schedule based on the last digit of the NIT, typically between 15 August and 15 October of the following tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT - Colombian tax identification number of the entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the local S.A.S. NIT. Foreign shareholders are not entered unless they have permanent establishment registration in Colombia.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares whether the taxpayer is a Free Trade Zone user subject to the 20% preferential rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select only if the Colombian entity holds a valid FTZ user certificate; non-resident parent status is irrelevant for this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from bonded warehouse operations, storage, and related logistics services before deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Colombian-source revenue generated by the local bonded depot. Payments received by the foreign parent for onsite services are not included unless attributable to a Colombian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 38 (Net Taxable Income before Special Deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed after costs, deductible expenses, FIT deductions, loss carryforwards, and FTZ preferential income adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the preferential 20% FTZ income regime only to eligible FTZ activities; any income from sales into the national customs territory must be separated and taxed at the standard 35% rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculates the tax due and identifies distributable profits for foreign dividend withholding purposes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should verify that the local entity reports accumulated profits from taxed income so subsequent dividend payments can enjoy the reduced 5% withholding rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a penalty equal to 5% per month or fraction of the tax assessed, capped at 100% of the tax due (Tax Statute Art. 641). DIAN may additionally impose fixed fines based on UVT and moratory interest, and may issue a formal assessment if the return is not filed after written notice.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% standard withholding on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders from profits that were already subject to Colombian corporate income tax; 10% if distributed from exempt or otherwise untaxed profits. These withholdings are final taxes for the foreign recipient.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced rate under an applicable double tax agreement (DTA), the foreign beneficial owner must provide the Colombian payer with a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction, apostilled or legalized as required, together with proof of beneficial ownership. The payer must retain the documentation and record the reduced rate in the monthly withholding return (Form 350). If the documentation is unavailable at payment date, the statutory rate must be withheld and a refund may be claimed before DIAN.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Colombian withholding tax on cross-border royalties and interest is 15.0%. Treaty relief may reduce these rates depending on the DTA, commonly to 10% for royalties and 10% or lower for interest, subject to TRC and beneficial ownership documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full local file and master file documentation is mandatory when any of the following thresholds are exceeded based on the applicable annual UVT (2025 UVT = COP 49,799): total gross assets >= 45,000 UVT (approx. COP 2,240,955,000), gross income >= 61,000 UVT (approx. COP 3,037,739,000), or aggregate related-party transactions >= 90,000 UVT (approx. COP 4,481,910,000). Lower-volume taxpayers with assets >= 4,500 UVT or income >= 8,000 UVT must still file the informative transfer pricing schedule (Form 120).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in certain offshore centres, but the GAAR and DIAN anti-abuse principles require genuine commercial substance for FTZ companies. A bonded depot must maintain physical premises in the FTZ, employees, operational records, inventory logs, and actual risk-bearing. Artificial arrangements lacking substance will be disregarded and the preferential FTZ rate denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing false Form 110 information, underreporting gross income from bonded storage, misclassifying national customs territory sales as FTZ income, or omitting assets held in the depot from the tax report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal imprisonment of 4 to 9 years plus restitution of the evaded tax and moratory interest; administrative penalty arrays include a 100% evasion surcharge and DIAN-determined additional tax checks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Law 1258 of 2008, courts may pierce the Limited Liability shield where the S.A.S. is used as a façade or vehicle for tax fraud. Directors who signed the false return face joint civil liability, criminal indictment, asset freezes, travel bans (anotación de salida del país), and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a nominal FTZ bonded depot without real warehouse staff, inventory controls, or customs compliance; creating interposed related-party storage invoicing solely to access the preferential 20% FTZ tax rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN will disallow the preferential rate retroactively, re-tax previously benefited profits at the standard 35% plus moratory interest, impose a 100% surcharge, and revoke the FTZ operating permit. Criminal anti-evasion action may also be initiated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing exposes directors and shareholders to the assessed tax liabilities, surcharges, and interest. Senior officers face direct criminal responsibility as co-planners or beneficiaries of the artificial scheme, including suspension from corporate management and exclusion from foreign trade privileges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement a lawful risk management system for Laundering and Terrorist Financing ('SARLAFT'), accepting cash above regulatory thresholds without client due diligence, or failing to identify beneficial owners of foreign shippers and warehouse end-customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines per transaction or per control failure as determined by the Superintendency of Ports and Transport and DIAN; criminal money laundering charges can result in imprisonment of 10 to 30 years and seizure of goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, legal representatives, and compliance officers are individually liable for failures in AML controls. Penalties include heavy personal fines, travel restrictions, disqualification from the cargo/warehouse sector and financial services, and imprisonment for wilful or grossly negligent misconduct.
